- [1.] For any $X \in P_0$ there exists a unique semi-perfect monomial $Y \in Q_0(\mathfrak{g})$ such that $T_0(X) = T_1(Y)$.

- [2.] Let $X=x_{1}x_{2}\cdots x_m$ with $x_i \in Q_0(\mathfrak{g})$, be a semi-perfect monomial. Then for any $s\in \{1, \ldots, m\}$ the monomial $X'=x_{1}\cdots x_{s-1} x_{s+1}\cdots x_m$ is also semi-perfect.

- [3.] There is a bijection $\psi: P_0 \rightarrow  S(\mathfrak{g})$: for every $X \in P_0$ there exists a unique $Y \in S(\mathfrak{g})$ such that $T_0(X) = T_1(\psi^{-1}(Y))$.

- [4.] The set of semi-perfect monomials $S^{(i)}(\mathfrak{g})$ is a basis of the vector space $U_0^{(i)}(\mathfrak{g})$.
card.label: Lemma 25

paper.title: Gelfand-Tsetlin modules for Lie algebras of rank $2$
paper.abstract: We explicitly construct families of simple modules for Lie algebras of rank $2$, on which certain commutative subalgebra acts diagonally and has a simple spectrum. In type $A$ these modules are well known generic Gelfand-Tsetlin modules and they can be viewed as such for other rank $2$ Lie algebras.
